resolution.rationale: Upstream v0.93.0 does not touch goal negotiation: goals stay AIR-only upstream and there is no provider-neutral opt-in, and docs/air-extensions.md is unchanged. Its src/acp-agent.ts edits add the adapter-handled /remote-control command (#1197) in the prompt path and run the v1 session/fork handler inside the new fork holds of the session list (#1368); neither reads or advertises the goal capability. The v0.91 adaptation c16a02cb2c98479194eab5e833a54f45d4e21a4c replays cleanly with an unchanged stable patch-id, and the goal tests pass on v0.93.0.
tests: npm run test:run -- src/tests/acp-agent.test.ts -t "advertises and publishes goals for an opted-in non-AIR client|publishes active_goal as provider-neutral session state without changing turn settlement|advertises async tasks with steering and goals for an opted-in non-AIR client"

resolution.rationale: Upstream async tasks remain AIR-only in v0.93.0, and clientSupportsAsyncTasks and its callers are unchanged. The new /remote-control command (#1197) refuses to run while foregroundWork or an unsettled turn exists; it does not depend on how async tasks were negotiated, so a non-AIR client that opted in with _meta["async-tasks"] is treated exactly like AIR with asyncTasks. The fork holds of #1368 are session index state only. The v0.91 adaptation 7f504014fe77d895a99adee24e3ca09d735b4eb8 replays cleanly with an unchanged stable patch-id; the async task, create-session-options (including the per-task stop affordance cases), tool call contract and native subagent suites pass with it.
tests: npm run test:run -- src/tests/async-tasks.test.ts src/tests/acp-agent.test.ts src/tests/create-session-options.test.ts src/tests/tool-call-contract.test.ts src/tests/native-subagents.test.ts
npm run test:run -- src/tests/create-session-options.test.ts -t "per-task stop affordance"

resolution.rationale: Upstream v0.93.0 still lists advisor_tool_result among the ignored content blocks of toAcpNotifications, so the patch is not absorbed. The v0.93.0 src/acp-agent.ts edits (/remote-control and the session/fork holds) do not touch the advisor path, and the patch still resolves the advisor server tool through the normal tool_result path. 590b7ed9e90414124c60eb0b853ad6ed4575a24c replays cleanly with an unchanged stable patch-id, and the incomplete-tool suite passes with it.

Upstream v0.93.0 has no _alas/context_usage request or contextUsage advertisement, and its package.json and package-lock.json change only the version, so Claude Agent SDK 0.3.300 and Query.getContextUsage({ detail }) are unchanged. The v0.93.0 src/acp-agent.ts edits do not touch the initialize advertisement or the request handler the patch adds. The v0.91 adaptation 1b1425052d7aa057e3d7ebaf84d1067b7c565a30 replays cleanly on top of the replayed async task adaptation with an unchanged stable patch-id, and both context usage tests pass.

resolution.rationale: Upstream v0.93.0 (#1368) holds a fork back from the session list until its session/fork response is out. In SessionIndexService.listSessions it adds a ForkHolds.isHeld filter before the sessionInfoOf map, the statement where this patch passes the negotiated row metadata key (this.deps.meta) to sessionInfoOf, so replaying 325c503f05cd7fb9ed98b7a05192b8afb6c8e164 conflicts only there. The replacement keeps both: held forks are filtered out, then each row is built with this.deps.meta. The other #1368 hunks (ForkHolds, forkHolds in the list subscription deps, forking/onForkCreated in the connection and both fork handlers) merge cleanly next to the patch's meta changes. ForkHolds lives in the service, which the patch creates for an AIR client with sessionIndex and for a client that opts in with _meta.sessionIndex, and rows released after the fork response go through the same deliver path that writes this.deps.meta. Upstream still gates the session index on AIR's sessionIndex, so the patch is not absorbed. A new test checks that a client with the neutral opt-in sees no fork in session/list or _session/list/changes before its session/fork response, and then gets it with forkedFrom under _meta.sessionIndex in both; it fails when session/list drops either the fork-hold filter or this.deps.meta. The replacement has a stable patch-id distinct from the retired commit.
tests: npm run test:run -- src/tests/session-index.test.ts -t "holds a fork back"
npm run test:run -- src/tests/session-index.test.ts src/tests/acp-scenarios.test.ts src/tests/prompt-suggestions.test.ts
